title: Notice Before Consent
text: Before or at the time of requesting consent, individuals must be clearly told what personal data is being collected, why it is being processed, and how they can exercise their rights or file a complaint.
mitigation_hint: Provide a clear, plain-language notice describing data collected, purpose, and complaint process before any data collection.

title: Valid Consent
text: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous, given through clear affirmative action, and limited only to the data necessary for the stated purpose.
mitigation_hint: Implement a clear opt-in consent mechanism limited strictly to data necessary for the specified purpose; avoid bundled or pre-ticked consent.

title: Right to Withdraw Consent
text: A person can withdraw consent at any time, and withdrawing should be as easy as giving it. Once withdrawn, further processing based on that consent must stop, though it does not affect processing done before withdrawal.
mitigation_hint: Add a simple, one-step withdrawal-of-consent option and stop processing promptly once consent is withdrawn.

title: Consent Manager Mechanism
text: Individuals may give, manage, review, or withdraw consent through a registered Consent Manager acting as a transparent, interoperable single point of contact.
mitigation_hint: Consider integrating with a registered Consent Manager platform for centralized consent handling.

title: Processing Without Explicit Consent
text: Personal data may be processed without fresh consent in specific legitimate situations, such as data voluntarily provided for a clear purpose, compliance with law, medical emergencies, public health measures, disasters, or employment-related needs.
mitigation_hint: Document which legitimate-use ground (if any) justifies processing where consent is not separately obtained.

title: Reasonable Security Measures
text: Organizations must implement reasonable technical and organizational security safeguards to protect personal data and prevent breaches, and must notify the Data Protection Board and affected individuals if a breach occurs.
mitigation_hint: Adopt encryption, access controls, and a documented breach-notification process covering both regulators and affected users.

title: Retention Limitation and Erasure
text: Personal data must be erased once its specified purpose is no longer being served or consent is withdrawn, unless retention is required by other law; the same erasure obligation extends to any processor handling the data.
mitigation_hint: Define a clear data retention period tied to purpose, and implement automatic erasure once that purpose ends or consent is withdrawn.

title: Data Accuracy and Completeness
text: Where personal data is used to make decisions affecting an individual or is shared with another organization, its completeness, accuracy, and consistency must be ensured.
mitigation_hint: Add validation and periodic data-accuracy checks, especially before decision-making or third-party sharing.

title: Grievance Mechanism
text: Organizations must publish contact details of a responsible officer and maintain an effective mechanism to address grievances from individuals about their personal data.
mitigation_hint: Publish a designated contact and set up a grievance-handling workflow with defined response timelines.

title: Processing Data of Children
text: Processing a child's personal data requires verifiable parental or guardian consent, must not harm the child's well-being, and must not involve behavioral tracking or targeted advertising directed at children.
mitigation_hint: Add age-verification and verifiable parental consent flows; disable tracking-based ads for users identified as minors.

title: Additional Obligations for Large-Scale Processors
text: Organizations designated as Significant Data Fiduciaries (based on data volume, sensitivity, or risk) must appoint an India-based Data Protection Officer, conduct independent data audits, and perform periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments.
mitigation_hint: If processing at scale or sensitive data, appoint a Data Protection Officer and schedule periodic DPIAs and independent audits.

title: Right to Access Personal Data
text: Individuals have the right to request a summary of what personal data is being processed about them and the identities of other parties with whom it has been shared.
mitigation_hint: Build a self-service or request-based mechanism for users to obtain a summary of their data and its sharing history.

title: Correction, Completion, and Erasure
text: Individuals can request correction, completion, updating, or erasure of their personal data, and the organization must act on such requests unless retention is legally required.
mitigation_hint: Provide an accessible process for users to request correction or deletion of their data, with clear turnaround times.

title: Data Principal's Right to Grievance Redressal
text: Individuals have the right to a readily available grievance redressal process, and organizations must respond within a prescribed period before the individual can escalate to the Data Protection Board.
mitigation_hint: Ensure grievance responses are issued within the prescribed timeline before escalation becomes necessary.

title: Right to Nominate
text: Individuals may nominate another person to exercise their data rights in case of their death or incapacity.
mitigation_hint: Offer a nomination feature allowing users to designate someone to manage their data rights if they become unable to.

title: Restrictions on Data Transfer Outside India
text: The government may restrict transfer of personal data to specific countries or territories outside India; transfers to non-restricted countries are otherwise generally permitted.
mitigation_hint: Check whether the destination country is restricted before transferring personal data outside India, and document the transfer basis.

title: Data Processor Obligations
text: A Data Fiduciary remains fully responsible for compliance even when personal data is processed by a third-party Data Processor on its behalf, and any such engagement must be under a valid contract.
mitigation_hint: Use written data-processing agreements with all vendors/processors and retain accountability for their compliance.

title: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Significant breaches of the Act can attract substantial monetary penalties, with the amount determined by factors such as severity, repetition, data sensitivity, and mitigation efforts taken by the organization.
mitigation_hint: Maintain evidence of proactive mitigation efforts, since demonstrated remediation can reduce penalty severity.

title: Definition of Personal Data Breach
text: A personal data breach includes any unauthorized processing, accidental disclosure, alteration, destruction, or loss of access to personal data that compromises its confidentiality, integrity, or availability.
mitigation_hint: Define internal breach criteria matching this definition so incidents are correctly identified and reported.

title: Applicability of the Act
text: The Act applies to digital personal data processed within India and to processing outside India if it relates to offering goods or services to individuals in India; purely personal/domestic use and publicly self-disclosed data are excluded.
mitigation_hint: Confirm whether the project falls within the Act's territorial scope before assuming exemption.
